prompt:
This directory holds a Python Markdown parser with a small command-line tool (markdown_it/cli/parse.py). The tool converts files given on the command line and otherwise starts an interactive prompt, so there is no way to pipe Markdown into it. Add a `--stdin` option. Expected behaviour: - `main(["--stdin"])` reads all Markdown from standard input, writes the rendered HTML to standard output exactly as converting a file would (for "# a b c" the output is "

a b c

\n"), and returns 0. Standard input must be read when main runs, not when the module is imported. - If standard input cannot be read, print a one-line message to standard error and exit with status 1. - File names given on the command line keep working as before and take priority; with no file names and no `--stdin` the interactive prompt still starts. - The option appears in the tool's --help text, and the usage example in README.md shows it. Do not edit any existing test file; put new tests in a new file under tests/. The existing suite (`python3 -m pytest tests`) must keep passing. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

rubric.criterion: The transcript shows the agent reading the command-line module (argument parser, main, file conversion) before editing and reusing the existing rendering path for standard input.
After editing, the agent ran the CLI tests or the whole suite and reports the result; new tests sit in a new file and exercise main with --stdin, the error path and the precedence of file names.
The change is small, follows the module's style, updates the README example as asked, and the final message lists the files changed and assumptions.
